lyrics.original:
[Intro]
Thunder on the county line, comin' low and slow...

[Verse 1]
I ran the interstate till the tank ran dry,
Chasing somethin' better under somebody's sky.
But every mile I burned just circled back to you,
And the map inside my chest only pointed one way through.

[Pre-Chorus]
So if the sky wants to open, let it open wide,
I ain't runnin' from the weather no more, no more tonight—

[Chorus]
Wash me in the Carolina rain,
Every crooked road, every mile of blame.
I'll stand here soakin', I'll say your name—
Come on and wash me in the Carolina rain.

[Verse 2]
I've got a temper like a match in a dry July,
Words I can't take back and a stubborn, foolish pride.
But I'd trade every hard thing I ever said,
For your hand on my shoulder and your rain on my head.

[Pre-Chorus]
So if the storm's gonna find me, let it find me here,
I'm done outrunnin' every cloud I ever feared—

[Chorus]
Wash me in the Carolina rain,
Every crooked road, every mile of blame.
I'll stand here soakin', I'll say your name—
Come on and wash me in the Carolina rain.

[Bridge]
When the levee breaks—
Let it break.
When my hands are shakin'—
Hold the ache.
There ain't no drought that love can't drown,
So let it come down, let it come down.

[Final Chorus]
Wash me in the Carolina rain,
Every crooked road, every mile of blame.
I'll stand here soakin', I'll say your name—
Come on and wash me... in the Carolina rain.

[Outro]
Let it come down, oh...
Wash me in the Carolina rain.
lyrics.tagged:
[Intro]
[Fingerpicked acoustic, dobro, clean electric swells]
[Female lead: low, smoky, close]
Thunder on the county line, comin' low and slow...

[Verse 1]
[Male lead: deep, gravelly baritone; intimate solo]
I ran the interstate till the tank ran dry,
Chasin' somethin' better under somebody's sky.
But every mile I burned just circled back to you,
And the map inside my chest knew what the blacktop never knew.

[Pre-Chorus]
[Male lead; mandolin and brushes enter]
So if the sky wants to open, let it open wide,
[Female joins in close upper harmony]
I ain't runnin' from the weather no more, no more tonight—

[Chorus]
[Male melody; female close harmony; full-band lift]
Wash me in the Carolina rain,
Every crooked road, every mile of blame.
[Male backing trio enters behind both leads]
I'll stand here soakin', I'll say your name—
Come on and wash me in the Carolina rain.

[Verse 2]
[Sparse acoustic, muted clean guitar, bass and brushes]
[Female lead: rich, smoky country soul; solo]
I've got a temper like a match in a dry July,
Words I can't take back and a stubborn, foolish pride.
But I'd trade every hard thing I ever said,
[Male adds soft low harmony beneath female melody]
For your hand on my shoulder and the rain on my head.

[Pre-Chorus]
[Female lead; fiddle answers between phrases]
So if the storm's gonna find me, let it find me here,
[Male joins in close lower harmony]
I'm done outrunnin' every cloud I ever feared—

[Chorus]
[Female melody; male lower harmony; stronger backbeat]
Wash me in the Carolina rain,
Every crooked road, every mile of blame.
[Male backing trio swells behind both leads]
I'll stand here soakin', I'll say your name—
Come on and wash me in the Carolina rain.

[Instrumental Break]
[Clean blues-funk guitar answered by fiddle and dobro]
[Sparse banjo and mandolin; keep the same slow pulse]

[Bridge]
[Acoustic, dobro, quiet foot-stomp; exposed voices]
[Male lead: low, rough, vulnerable]
When the levee breaks—
[Female lead: tender answer]
Let it break.
[Female lead: intimate solo]
When my hands are shakin'—
[Male lead: reassuring answer]
Hold the ache.
[Both leads in close harmony; backing trio enters softly]
There ain't no drought that love can't drown,
[All voices build; ragged edges, controlled power]
So let it come down, let it come down.

[Final Chorus]
[Full band; dirty accents beneath audible clean guitar]
[Male melody; female upper harmony; male backing trio]
Wash me in the Carolina rain,
[Female melody; male lower harmony; backing trio sustains]
Every crooked road, every mile of blame.
[Both leads harmonize; backing trio swells behind them]
I'll stand here soakin', I'll say your name—
Come on and wash me... in the Carolina rain.

[Outro]
[Acoustic guitar and dobro only]
[Male lead: low, raspy, unforced]
Let it come down, oh...
[Both leads: soft close harmony; backing trio fades]
Wash me in the Carolina rain.
[Let the last dobro note ring]

variants.label: Balanced Carolina soul
variants.hypothesis: Establish clean-guitar identity, distinct co-leads, and restrained roots grit.
held_constant: Two co-leads and supporting male trio
variants.style: Soulful Carolina country duet with grungegrass grit and 1990s unplugged-rock tension. 78 BPM, slow 12/8, deep pocket. Two leads: deep, chesty male baritone with sandpaper rasp, tender lows and ragged soulful belts; rich, smoky female country lead with clear, ringing highs. Alternate solo verse blocks; share choruses in close harmony. Male backing trio: bright high tenor, smoky middle, resonant low harmony; tight country thirds, rough rock edge at peaks, always behind both leads. Prominent clean single-coil guitar: fingerstyle funk, muted ghost notes, blues bends, double-stops. Acoustic flatpicking, sparse banjo rolls, mandolin chops, crying fiddle and dobro, woody bass, subtle B3. Brushed drums build to heavy backbeat; dirty guitar swells lift choruses without masking clean guitar. Earthy Carolina drawl, porch intimacy, pick attack, warm live-room sound. Aching to redemptive; exposed call-response bridge, huge final harmonies, bare acoustic outro.
variants.exclude: hard-tuned robotic vocals, metal screaming, EDM drops, trap drums, breakneck bluegrass, novelty hoedown
